description: Independent, modern implementations of the J and APL array languages: parallel and vectorized, embeddable from Rust, Python, and C
rules: The PyPI package and CLI are named libjay, but the Python import is jay (like pillow/PIL): pip install libjay, then import jay.
Braces in a program string always bind data ({name} is a parameter), never splice text into the program.
jay.j(...) and jay.apl(...) compile, bind and execute in one call; jay.j.compile(...) returns a reusable kernel with .bind() for defaults.

The APL implemented is the APL2/ISO line verified against GNU APL; trains and function assignment are extensions on by default, and Dyalog-specific readings are a planned dialect switch, not the default.
DataFrames map to a matrix rows-leading: J +/ sums each column, +/"1 sums each row; Arrow/numpy int64 and float64 columns cross zero-copy.
Columns with nulls or mixed numeric types are refused with an error naming the column; cast or fill explicitly rather than expecting coercion.
Errors point into the source string; 'not supported yet' means planned, 'not in the language' and 'closed by the sandbox' mean permanent.
Use kernel.explain() or libjay --explain to see how an expression parsed, what fused, and per-node result shapes.
